4.3.4.4 Accessing NvM in multicore/multipartition configurations
A system using multiple cores or EcucPartitions may map NVBlocks to a specific
EcucPartition. Based on these mappings, an RTE shall implement protection (such
as the use of IOC or CallTrustedFunction) to cross partition protection boundaries
in certain circumstances.
NVBlocks are mapped to a specific partition through the use of the ECUC parameter
NvMBlockEcucPartitionRef [ECUC_NvM_00564] which is set on an NvMBlock-
Descriptor.
[SWS_Rte_03897]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00176, SRS_Rte_00177
⌈The RTE Generator shall reject configurations where the EcucPartition which ref-
erences an NvBlockSwComponentType (via ECUC parameter EcucPartition-
SoftwareComponentInstanceRef) does not match the EcucPartition refer-
enced by all NvMBlockDescriptors (via the ECUC parameter NvMBlockEcucPar-
titionRef) associated with that NvBlockSwComponentType.⌋
Note: NvMBlockDescriptors associated with an NvBlockSwComponentType can
be found via the ECUC container RteNvRamAllocation. Specifically, NvBlock-
Descriptors are aggregated by an NvBlockSwComponentType, which are then
mapped to a corresponding NvMBlockDescriptor (from the NvM) by an RteN-
vRamAllocation via the ECUC parameters RteSwNvBlockDescriptorRef and
RteNvmBlockRef.
[SWS_Rte_03898]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00176, SRS_Rte_00177
⌈The RTE Generator shall support configurations where a VariableDataPrototype
instance in the role NvBlockDescriptor.ramBlock of a NvBlock
